label: text
text: The owners' new wage offer, on an eight-hours' day basis, will to-morrow and Tuesday have been posted in all districts.

label: text
text: The first announcements published in the Warwickshire coal fields indicate that in some districts wages will be increased, instead of decreased, as compared with the pre-stoppage rates.

label: text
text: Whereas the owners gave an undertaking to the Prime Minister that the new terms should be guaranteed for three months, the Warwickshire owners make their offer for nine months. Under this offer the wages of a piece worker, when working on a minimum day rate, will be increased from 10/3 to 10/10 per shift and those of a day worker from 8/11 to 9/5.

label: text
text: A number of other classes of men will get a slight increase, whilst the lowest rate that an underground man can earn will remain at 8/6 per shift and that of surface men at 8/.-British Wireless Service.

label: text
text: The debates on the coal dispute which have occupied practically the whole time of the House of Commons during the week have to some extent elucidated a complicated situation. It has been at last made clear that the Government will stand by the Coal Commission's report, and is carrying out measures which it recommended should be placed on the Statutebook; and that so soon as the other parties show willingness to do the same the Government will foster negotiations by every possible means.

label: text
text: As to the Eight-Hours Bill, it is pointed out that this measure does not affect the acceptance of the report one way or the other. It simply removes an impediment to any negotiations involving an alteration in working hours, by making it permissible for the men to agree to work for a longer period. The miners remain as free as they were to make a settlement with or without alteration of hours.—British Wireless.

label: text
text: Private advices from London to local coal authorities indicate an early settlement of the strike seems hardly probable. This is confirmed by the British Government Coal Committee placing additional orders for 300,000 tons of American coal.—Reuter.

label: text
text: Linton Wells, an American world-circler, passed Osaka at 9-4 a.m. to-day by train for Yokohama, where the Empress of Asia is awaiting to accommodate him. It is expected he will return to New York on the 12th inst., successfully completing the trip in twenty-seven days.—Router.

label: text
text:
Mexico City, July 3.
Continued torrential rains are rendering the flood conditions in Mexico most serious. Despatches from Salvatierra describe the situation as desperate. It is reported in the Central Plateau, known as the "granary of Mexico," the crops are virtually ruined, the railway flooded in sections and the permanent way torn up. Many bridges have been destroyed and telegraph lines are down—Reuter.
[An earlier cable stated: —A message from Leon, Mexico, says the flood havoc had been aggravated by an outbreak of plague. Six thousand families are homeless and foodless. Relief trains are coming in slowly but supplies are inadequate. Looting has begun in spite of a military cordon round the district. The total bodies recovered number 250, many with clothing torn off by the forces of water.]

label: text
text: Some amazing flying was witnessed at the Royal Air Force pageant at Hendon yesterday by Their Majesties the King and Queen, King Alfonso and Queen Ena, of Spain, and many other members of the Royal Houses, members of the Cabinet, numerous Military and Air Attaches of Foreign Lowers, and by over 100,000 of the public.

label: text
text: Nearly 200 aeroplanes of different designs took part, and gave a seven-hours' exposition of the whole art of flying.

label: text
text: One of the most impressive spectacles was the Royal salute by 54 aeroplanes in close formation and precise alignment, followed by remarkable evolutions with the tips of the wings almost touching.

label: text
text: Several types of machines not hitherto seen in public were shown, including the latest night bomber, and a coastal torpedo plane which carries a 21-inch topedo. besides machine-guns, and has a great speed, together with a Hornbill single-seater fighter of a most aggressive nature, with a 700 horse-power Rolls Royce Condor engine, which climbs with unprecedented rapidity.

label: text
text: The tailless aeroplane and the helicopter also participated in the display, these being part of the experimental equipment of the Air Research Department.

label: text
text: The air manœuvres of the fighter squadron were directed by radio telephone and gave ample evidence of the progress of highly important air drill. The words of command from the ground to the squadron leader in the air, and repeated by him to his officers, were heard distinctly by crowds from Marconiphone loud speakers.

label: text
text: The four pilots who recently flew "in Fairey machines" from Cairo to the Cape and back to Britain absolutely to schedule time, covering 56,000 miles without a hitch; were given a warm welcome.

label: text
text: The possibilities of the modern fighting machine were displayed by daring dives, loops, and rolls of some of the air officers, and a display of bom's dropping was also given.

label: text
text: There was no accident of any kind in spite of the nature of the feats performed and the presence of so many machines close together. — British Wireless Service.

label: text
text: Thousands of schoolboys and girls were invited to attend the final rehearsal at Hendon yesterday of the annual Royal Air Force display, which is being witnessed to-day by King George and Queen Mary, the King and Queen of Spain, Prince Chichibu of Japan, and Air Attaches of numerous nations.

label: text
text: Nearly two hundred machines, including many of new and latest types, are participating in the exhibition, which will be notable for precision of manoeuvre and efficiency of control by wireless telephony system.—British Wireless.

label: text
text: There is no mention of a capital 'evy' or compulsory mobilisation of securities in the report of the official Committee of experts appointed to formulate a financial programme, which recommends Parliament temporarily to waive certain prerogatives regarding expenditure.

label: text
text: M. Canaux is given a greater degree of control in financial matters, the Committee urging retrenchment of expenditure and the revision of the sugar, drink, and business turnover taxes, and the immediate conclusion of the debt funding agreements with Great Britain and America, after which long-term loans will be negotiated.

label: text
text: The franc will ultimately be stabilised at a figure between the cost of living index and the prevailing market rate of the franc. "Reuter.

label: text
text:
The report of the committee of experts' comprises 54 foolscap pages besides technical appendices.
It emphasises that the recommendations must be taken as a whole.

label: text
text: The most striking passage says that the financial reconstruction is bound to cause a grave economic crisis momentarily. The stabilisation of exchange will involve a rise in home prices. Increased production costs will reduce exports. The bankruptcy of firms artificially enriched by the fall of the franc will ensue, and unemployment is inevitable, but the sooner and the more effectively the situation is faced the shorter will be the crisis.

label: text
text: France must depend primarily on her own efforts to restore the financial situation. The task is not in-surmountable, but it will be long and painful.

label: text
text:
The Committee are unanimously
of opinion that the measures they
advise are calculated to ensure
righting the position.

label: text
text: The recommendations include the raising of the Customs duties. The opinion is expressed that the report will strengthen the hand of M. Caillaux.—Reuter.
